blogs.title: How Language Models Are Becoming Feature Engineers – A Primer
blogs.description: This post breaks down the idea that Large Language Models (LLMs) can replace traditional feature engineering for tabular data. It explains the core concept behind FeatLLM, how LLMs generate rule‑based features from few examples, and why this matters for low‑shot learning scenarios.

blogs.title: From Rules to Predictions: Inside FeatLLM’s Two‑Step Reasoning Engine
blogs.description: Dive deep into the structured prompt design used by FeatLLM. The article walks readers through the three key prompt components (basic info, reasoning instruction, response instruction), showing concrete examples of how an LLM infers causal relationships and produces clean, parseable rules.

blogs.title: Why FeatLLM Beats Other LLM‑Based Tabular Models on Real‑World Datasets
blogs.description: This comparison‑heavy post reviews FeatLLM’s performance against baselines like XGBoost, TabLLM, and TABLET across 13 diverse datasets. It discusses inference costs, prompt‑size limitations, and the robustness that comes from rule bagging and ensemble techniques.

blogs.title: Low‑Shot Tabular Learning Made Practical: Tips for Deploying FeatLLM in Industry
blogs.description: Targeted at practitioners, this guide covers the practical side of using FeatLLM: choosing an LLM API, setting temperature and top‑p, managing ensemble size, evaluating feature quality, and handling spurious correlations. It also touches on future directions such as extending to larger datasets and ensuring interpretability.
